m23.content:
The bug is in `com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.IRFactory.handleBlockComment(com.google.javascript.rhino.head.ast.Comment)`.

The method only reports `SUSPICIOUS_COMMENT_WARNING` when `comment.getValue()` contains one of two exact substrings:

```java
"/* @"
"\n * @"
```

That heuristic is too narrow. It misses suspicious block comments where the annotation is formatted with slightly different whitespace, which is exactly what these tests cover:

- `/* \n *@type {number} */`
- indented `* @type` lines
- later `* @type` lines after other text

Static evidence:
- [`IRFactory.handleBlockComment`](com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.IRFactory.handleBlockComment(com.google.javascript.rhino.head.ast.Comment)) only does those two literal `indexOf(...)` checks.
- [`IRFactory.transformTree`](com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.IRFactory.transformTree(com.google.javascript.rhino.head.ast.AstRoot, com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.StaticSourceFile, java.lang.String, com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.Config, com.google.javascript.rhino.head.ErrorReporter)) routes all `BLOCK_COMMENT`s through that method.

Dynamic evidence:
- Runtime verification hit `handleBlockComment` from `ParserTest.testSuspiciousBlockCommentWarning3`.
- The condition at line 252 evaluated false and execution skipped the `warning(...)` call entirely, confirming an incorrect branch on a failing test input.

So the root cause is a logic error in the suspicious-comment detector: it relies on exact spacing patterns instead of recognizing `@type`-style annotations more flexibly inside block comments.
